To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Emotional stimuli engage specific cognitive processes and neural systems that enhance explicit memory.

(1) Emotional arousal influences explicit memory via factors that operate during memory encoding and factors that modulatememory consolidation; (2) The amygdala plays a key role in the enhancement of memory for emotional stimuli via modulation of encoding and/or consolidation processes; (3) The amygdalar role in memory enhancement is likely due to the engagement of specific cognitive mechanisms that influence the encoding and/or consolidation of emotionally arousing information.
Emotional stimuli enhance explicit memory for both positive and negative emotional stimuli, and the amygdala plays a central role in the enhancement of explicit memory for emotional stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how emotional stimuli are encoded, consolidated and retrieved, and how the neural mechanisms involved in these processes interact with other cognitive processes.
the cognitive and neural mechanisms of memory for emotional stimuli and the implications of this research for our understanding of the neural basis of memory and emotion.
understanding the mechanisms by which emotional arousal enhances explicit memory and how this process may contribute to the formation of emotional memories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
emotional arousal enhances explicit memory through the engagement of cognitive mechanisms (i.e., attention and elaboration) that are mediated by the amygdala.
emotional arousal enhances explicit memory through modulation of attention, elaboration and consolidation processes and that this effect is mediated by the amygdala.

emotional memory is enhanced through the interaction of attention, elaboration, and consolidation factors, and that the amygdala is a critical component of the neural circuitry that supports these processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amygdala is a critical node in the network that enhances memory for emotional information, and the mechanisms by which it does so are beginning to be understood.
emotional arousal influences explicit memory via a complex set of cognitive mechanisms and that the amygdala is the key brain structure that coordinates this influence.
the amygdala modulates memory for emotional stimuli via a combination of attention and memory consolidation mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amygdala is a key structure in the neural network that supports the encoding and consolidation of emotional memory.
emotional arousal enhances explicit memory by modulating the neural systems that support encoding and consolidation processes, with the amygdala playing a central role.
explicit memory for emotionally arousing events is highly adaptive, as it allows us to remember important events that are relevant for our survival.
